key_insight: Separating LLM-based extraction from deterministic score logic lets a clinical assistant treat missing information as unknown—not normal—so it asks fewer, more useful questions without losing accuracy.
clinical_relevance: For risk-score workflows, this approach can reduce under-triage and avoid premature decisions when chart notes are incomplete, while still supporting practical bedside use.
method: LLM extracts findings as present / absent / unknown
Code computes risk-score bounds over unknown inputs
Ask only questions that could change the decision
evidence_signal: Across 1,200 synthetic emergency cases and six calculators, the bounds policy matched ask-all accuracy (99.4%) with about half as many questions, and a 9B local extractor reached 99.8% accuracy.
watch_item: Results rely partly on synthetic cases and simulated clinician answers, so real-world performance may vary when documentation is messy or workflows differ.
paper_title: Unknown is not normal: separating language-model extraction from rule-based decision logic for clinical risk scores
